question: Norovirus is wreaking havoc on oyster farmers in Arcachon Bay and Brittany where oysters are regularly contaminated, making them unfit for consumption by causing gastroenteritis.1 The virus spreads particularly during wet periods when the inundation of rain water sewer systems results in sewage containing faeces overflowing from detention basins into the sea.

The problem is that municipalities and joint municipal groupings do not always have sufficient financial means to change underground pipes, construct larger spillways and expand water treatment plants. French authorities have already received two payments, most recently on 22 December 2023, under the national recovery plan to modernise drinking water and sewage systems. 1.
Is the Commission aware of any initiatives on the part of the French State within this recovery plan to modernise sewage systems in coastal municipalities near shellfish farms?
If necessary, could the Commission propose modifying the recovery plan to incorporate increased aid to these municipalities?
answer: 1. Following France’s second payment request submitted in July 2023, the Commission has assessed among others target 211 on secure water networks. The objective of this target was to start the renovation works for 450 kilometres of drinking water or sanitation networks in France, including the overseas departments (DOM), and the sanitisation of more than 6 500 tonnes of dry sewage sludge, by 31 December 2022. 2.
The target was positively assessed during the second payment request, disbursed in December 2023. The revision of the recovery and resilience plans come at the initiative of the Member State.
